learning_outcomes.text: The student will be introduced to the basic concepts and techniques of linear algebra and Euclidean geometry.
The student will be able to: i) solve systems of linear equations, ii) simple exercises of analytic geometry in space; operate on vectors and matrices; iii) diagonalize operators and matrices.
The student must be able to understand the rightness of the results obtained by himself or by others.
The student acquires scientific vocabulary. At the end of the course, the student is expected to be able to communicate mathematical arguments.
The student who has attended the course will be able to deepen his knowledge of linear algebra and vector spaces.

syllabus_topics: Elements of analytic geometry of the 3-dimensional space.
Parametric and cartesian equations of a straight line.
Wedge product and its fundamental properties.
Linear combination of vectors: linear dependence/independence.
Generators, bases and dimension of a vector space.
Determinants: definition using the formulas of Laplace and fundamental properties.
Elementary operations of the row and column of a matrice.
System of linear equations: Gauss-Jordan's theorem and Theorem of Rouche-Capelli.
Definition of the kernel and of image, Dimension's theorem, matrix associated to a linear application and rule base change.
Endomorphisms of a vector space: eigenvalues, eigenvectors and eigenspaces.
Algebraic multiplicity and geometry of an eigenvalue.
Diagonalization of symmetric matrices: the spectral theorem.
teaching_methods: Lectures (material presentation, formal definitions and proofs, abstract concepts illustrated through significant examples, applications, and exercises)
Guided sessions to discuss and solve exercises and assignments (within "Progetto IDEA")
assessment_rules: Course grades are based on a final exam comprising a preliminary multiple-choice test, a written exam, and an oral interview. The oral examination is optional for students who score more than 21 on the final written examination. The multiple-choice test has 10 questions and lasts 35 minutes, while the written exam includes 4 open-ended exercises and lasts 105 minutes. During the oral interview, students must demonstrate proper mathematical language and formalism.
bibliography: M. Abate, C. De Fabritiis, Geometria analitica con elementi di algebra lineare, 2a ed., Mc Graw-Hill, 2010.
